cards.explanation: The answer is Shiloh, friends. The whole congregation of Israel assembles there and sets up the Tent of Meeting (Joshua 18:1). Every tribe in one place, and everybody knows where to look for the Tent. That's a gathering with a clear address.

The answer is that seven tribes haven't received their inheritance, friends. Even though the land is subdued before them, there are still seven tribes of Israel who haven't yet received their inheritance (Joshua 18:1-2). Winning the land is one thing. Handing it out is another. Seven tribes are still standing there with empty hands.

The answer is False, friends. Joshua never asks about a hurry. Seven tribes had not yet received their inheritance (Joshua 18:2), and he asks, "How long will you put off entering and possessing the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?" (Joshua 18:3). That's a how-long question, and I know a few of those myself.

The answer is three, friends. Joshua tells the Israelites to appoint three men from each tribe (Joshua 18:4). Seven tribes, three men each, and not one of them could say "I thought you had the map." The text says they went throughout the land, mapping it city by city into seven portions, then came back with the document (Joshua 18:9). That's a whole land on paper. I can barely finish one cookie box without checking the recipe twice.

The answer is to survey the land and map it out, friends. Joshua says he will send them out "…survey the land and map it out, according to the inheritance of each." (Joshua 18:4). Then they return to him and divide the land into seven portions (Joshua 18:4-5). Looking, walking and writing it all down.

The answer is to cast lots before the LORD, friends. Joshua says, "…I will cast lots for you here in the presence of the LORD our God." (Joshua 18:6). The portions get mapped out and brought to him first. Then he casts the lots right there in the LORD's presence.

The answer is priesthood, friends. Joshua says the Levites have no portion among them "…because their inheritance is the priesthood of the LORD." (Joshua 18:7). They don't get a slice of land like the others. What they get is serving the LORD.

The answer is True, friends. Joshua says Gad, Reuben and half the tribe of Manasseh have already received the inheritance that Moses the servant of the LORD gave them beyond the Jordan to the east (Joshua 18:7). Their land is already settled. So they're not waiting in this drawing.

The answer is a document mapping the land, friends. The men went throughout the land, mapping it city by city into seven portions, then returned with the document to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh (Joshua 18:9). Seven portions, all written down. Now Joshua has something in hand to cast lots over.

The answer is Joshua son of Nun, friends, the very man running this whole land-dividing operation. The Israelites gave him an inheritance among them when they had finished distributing the land (Joshua 19:49). He handled everybody else's portion first, and his came after.
The answer is False, friends. The Israelites gave Joshua the city "…as the LORD had commanded." (Joshua 19:50). So the LORD's command stands behind this gift. It wasn't just the people's idea.

The answer is that Joshua asked for it, friends. The Israelites gave him the city of Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim "…as he requested." (Joshua 19:50). After handing out everyone else's land, the man had one request of his own. And he got it.

The answer is rebuilds, friends. Joshua "…rebuilt the city and settled in it." (Joshua 19:50). Both things are right there in one verse. He wasn't just handing out land for everybody else, because he put his hands to his own city too.

The answer is True, friends. Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families distributed these inheritances by lot to the tribes of Israel at Shiloh before the LORD (Joshua 19:51). Priest, leader and family heads all in on it. Everybody had a hand in it, and the LORD's presence was right there.
